item.title: Tennessee fined $250,000 after fans threw mustard and golf balls at coach
item.description: The Southeastern Conference has fined Tennessee $250,000 after fans threw a slew of objects toward LSU and their coach Lane Kiffin during a game the Volunteers won 27-13. SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey announced the penalty under the league's sportsmanship, game management and alcohol availability policies on Sunday. The trouble began with 3:14 remaining in the game when supporters in the Tennessee student section threw golf balls toward the Tigers bench. Play was halted for several minutes while the objects flew, and players gathered near the middle of the field to keep clear of any direct hits. Tennessee Volunteers fans react during the first half of the game against the LSU Tigers at Neyland Stadium on November 21, 2026 (Getty Images) “The golf balls have started being thrown at Neyland Stadium,” sports reporter Rhiannon Potkey wrote alongside video from the game. SportsCenter shared additional footage of a Tennessee staff member then carried a handful of golf balls and a mustard bottle to the sidelines. A message on the giant screen urged fans: “Keep your composure and practice good sportsmanship.” Kiffin ordered his players to exit through a side entrance once the game had finished rather than expose them to the home crowd a second time. “If cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues, the institution is subject to an immediate fine and suspension of the alcohol sales privilege," SEC rules state. The league has decided not to suspend alcohol sales at Tennessee for now, but it retains the right to do so in future. The hostility from Volunteers fans toward Kiffin stretches back to 2009, when he spent a single year as the university's head coach before leaving for USC. He came back for the first time in 2021, by then in charge of Ole Miss, and Kiffin and the Rebels were pelted with debris on that occasion too, some of it golf balls and a mustard bottle. Jeremiah Telander #22 of the Tennessee Volunteers celebrates after a 27-13 victory against the LSU (Getty Images) Tennessee students burned mattresses after Kiffin's departure, and in 2010 a Knoxville lawyer suggested renaming a wastewater treatment facility as the “Lane Kiffin Sewage Plant.” Tennessee coach Josh Heupel was asked about Kiffin's return, now as LSU head coach, during SEC media days this summer and referred back to the 2021 incident. “I certainly hope our fan base hasn’t cooled off.” Heupel said. “Whether it’s the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard or our sports stores, making sure that they got reinforcements on the golf balls ... hopefully Knoxville’s ready for his arrival.” The fine is Tennessee's second in quick succession, after the SEC fined the school $500,000 a month ago for allowing fans to storm the field following a 26-10 victory over then-No. 6 Alabama. item.title: Rejoice! Luca Williams-Barnett’s assist has officially been credited on appeal!
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: Luca Williams-Barnett of Tottenham Hotspur during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Ipswich Town at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on November 21, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images I did not realize this had happened until it was already over this morning, but apparently after Saturday’s Tottenham Hotspur win over Ipswich Town, Luca Williams-Barnett was NOT credited with a goal and an assist to Dominic Solanke — just the goal. Stat trackers Opta initially did not give the assist to Williams-Barnett as it was initially judged to have taken a very slight deflection off of Ipswich keeper Christian Walton. However, after review, Opta has officially reversed course and has issued Luca his assist, and even posted about how that made him the second youngest player to ever score and assist in a Premier League game. However, to hear him tell it, it was James Maddison who pressured Opta to begin with. After the match, Madders apparently emailed Opta to ask why Williams-Barnett didn’t get credited with the assist, and then followed up on social media to take “credit” for Opta switching gears. I’ve watched the highlights of LWB’s assist many times over the past couple of days and I have to say I had no idea it initially wasn’t granted, because it’s so obviously an assist that it never crossed my mind. So kudos to Opta for looking at the evidence and officially making Luca second to Michael Owen in a trivia category. That’s pretty heady company to be keeping, and hopefully he’ll continue to do great things while at Tottenham.

item.title: York repeats as state volleyball champion while Victor, Mercy fall short
item.description: GREIGSVILLE – York accomplished what most high school girls volleyball programs only dream of: Back-to-back state championships. The Golden Knights defeated Hamilton (Section III) in straight sets (25-15, 25-16, 25-19) Nov. 21 to win the 2026 NYSPHSAA Class D title at Harding Mazzotti Arena in Glens Falls. They received a champion’s welcome upon returning home to Livingston County. Bailey Orman was awarded most valuable player of the Class D state tournament for the second consecutive year. The junior also reached a personal milestone in Glens Falls – 1,000 career kills. A parade of fire trucks from Cuylerville, Leicester and York accompanied Orman and the Golden Knights’ return home. Dozens of fans cheered – many waving yellow towels – as they deboarded a school bus with championship plaque in hand. “We didn’t really get into a groove until the very end of the season,” York coach Kaitlin Kolb said. “We worked hard over the postseason to keep meshing together and play our roles to the best of our ability. It really came together in the finals.” Welcome home York earned its spot in the Class D final by finishing 2-1 in pool play. Despite its loss to Candor (IV), York advanced with wins over Hamilton and Duanesburg (II). JJ Kane recorded a whopping 25 digs in the championship match, adding five kills and four assists. Tessa Goodell distributed 23 assists while Bree Parsons logged 13 kills, five digs and three blocks. Orman totaled 12 kills, 10 digs and two blocks against Hamilton. CC Biondo had 11 digs, Jordan Ray added 10 digs, and Fiona Grant chipped in four kills and four digs for York. “We have a great support system,” said Parsons, a senior. “I think that’s one of the reasons we’ve gotten so far – they were always here to support us. Being able to celebrate with them is so great.” Biondo and Kane led York’s defense all weekend, finishing with 40 and 36 digs, respectively, in pool play. Goodell, meanwhile, orchestrated the offense at setter, dishing out 51 assists in pool play to go with her 21 digs. Parsons and Orman each totaled 20 kills in pool play. Orman, who also had 20 digs, recorded her 1,000 th career kill. “My parents and all the people I started my career with,” Orman said, “have really helped me grow and gotten me over some challenging times.” Parsons and Goodell joined Orman on the Class D all-tournament team. Biondo won the sportsmanship award. “It still feels so unreal even though it’s the second time we’ve experienced it,” said Biondo, a senior. “Each year is so unique because we all need to learn about each other on and off the court. It makes a big difference when you do make those connections." Leaving a legacy York defeated Candor in the 2025 Class D state final. item.title: Rennie gets backing despite All Black defeats
item.description: Dave Rennie took the All Blacks role following the departure of Scott Robertson [Getty Images] All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has received the unequivocal backing of his bosses at New Zealand Rugby to lead the team through to next year's World Cup. Rennie's side have suffered back-to-back defeats in the November leg of the Nations Championship and have lost five times in the calendar year for the first time since 1998. "We have complete confidence in him," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "His position is not in question. He will take the team to the World Cup. That is not going to change." Rennie was appointed in March and started his All Blacks tenure in style, dispatching France and Ireland in the July part of the Nations Championship before a memorable victory over world champions South Africa in the Springboks' spiritual home of Ellis Park. But New Zealand lost the next three Tests against the Boks to fall 3-1 in the 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' [RGR] series, and, although two convincing wins over Australia retained the Bledisloe Cup, the All Blacks have endured a difficult tour of Europe. A first loss to Wales in 73 years was followed by an English rout in Twickenham, while the All Blacks have also been hit by the tragic death of their long-serving head of security Logan Cadwallader. The emotional toll of Cadwaller's passing along with the arduous schedule this year are thought to be two mitigating factors behind the dip in form, and New Zealand's administrators will review the impact of the RGR series when planning its return in 2030. Lancaster added that the union will look to make a call in the middle of next year as to whether Rennie takes charge of the team beyond the 2027 World Cup. "We will conduct a full campaign and season review following this year, as we always do," he said. "That will inform how we approach next year, but it will also inform our discussions around what the contract situation looks like beyond next year. "Our intention is to make all those decisions and have clarity before we go into the World Cup. Nothing has changed from when we appointed [Rennie] earlier this year. "He is a world-class coach. We went through the most rigorous appointment process that I have been involved in, which included spending time observing him coaching in Japan with his team and in his environment." We let the country down - All Blacks coach Rennie

item.title: YouTube Star Secures Shock DP World Tour Invite
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images YouTube content creator Peter Finch has accepted a surprise sponsor invite to play the AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open on the DP World Tour. The event begins on December 10 and features a field that includes two-time Masters champion Bubba Watson. Finch, who runs a channel with over 850,000 subscribers, will compete against multiple tour winners in this 72-hole stroke play event. Finch announced the opportunity to his Instagram followers on Nov. 20, confirming that he will make his DP World Tour debut at the AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open. The opportunity was not entirely new: Finch had discussed receiving the sponsor exemption on his Rough Cut Golf Podcast in October. The Path to the Field Finch’s journey to the professional stage has been steady but difficult. Finch has some professional tournament experience, including a tied-50th finish at the 2025 Egyptian Open on the Asian Development Tour. He also reached Final Qualifying for The Open in 2025 and finished tied for sixth at the 2026 Fairmont St Andrews Classic on the Tartan Pro Tour. The Mauritius Open will represent a significant step up in competition. These results showed he could handle pressure, yet the DP World Tour invite remains a step up in class. The tournament field features plenty of proven talent. South African stars Branden Grace, Thriston Lawrence and Dean Burmester are multiple DP World Tour winners. Casey Jarvis, another rising South African star with multiple tour victories, will also compete. They will be joined by Bubba Watson and defending champion Jayden Schaper. Regarding the opportunity, Finch wrote on Instagram, “I cannot wait to get out to Mauritius and compete against some of the best players in the world!” He noted that he has followed the event for a long time and sees this as a major milestone. “I remember watching this tournament over the years and just thinking what an amazing spectacle and an amazing privilege it would be to play at these courses, and that’s what we’re going to be doing,” Finch added in his post. Content Creation Meets Competition This dual role as competitor and creator adds a unique layer to the tournament narrative. While other players focus solely on their scorecards, Finch will be documenting the experience for his large online audience. Finch’s documentation of the experience could bring new eyes to the DP World Tour and highlight the challenges facing the sport. Finch’s participation also highlights the growing overlap between golf’s traditional professional tours and its enormous online content community. His tournament videos could give viewers an unusual look at the pressures of competing in a DP World Tour event. With more than 851,000 YouTube subscribers, Finch could introduce the tournament to golf fans who might not otherwise follow the DP World Tour. item.title: Stock Watch: Which players impressed during Week 11 vs. Cardinals?
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs hosted the Arizona Cardinals in an important Week 11 matchup at Arrowhead Stadium, hoping to extend their winning streak to three games. The offense maintained a balanced attack, led by running back Emmett Johnson and veteran Travis Kelce, who scored twice. Patrick Mahomes spread the ball around, with Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen making plays alongside Rashee Rice at wide receiver. Xavier Worthy showcased his speed with an impressive fourth-quarter touchdown. The defense was ready, knowing the Cardinals had many issues, especially at quarterback. George Karlaftis tallied two more sacks, including a strip-fumble, in the victory. Nohl Williams was dominant in coverage, disrupting plays and showing versatility in the pass rush. Harrison Butker was perfect on the day, with two field goals silencing more critics and helping secure the team's victory. Check out how some of Kansas City's stars fared in the Chiefs' victory over the Cardinals: Stock Up: Travis Kelce The star tight end was in vintage form on Sunday with 6 catches for 74 yards and 2 touchdowns. He had his first game with multiple receiving touchdowns since Week 11 of 2022. Stock Up: Patrick Mahomes Mahomes was impressive again in Week 11, showing little concern for the Cardinals' defense. He finished the day with 27 completions, 324 yards, and 3 touchdowns. Stock Up: George Karlaftis The Chiefs pass rusher continues his Pro Bowl-worthy campaign, securing 2.5 sacks and one forced fumble on Josh Johnson, breathing more life into the once-criticized defensive line. Stock Up: Nohl Williams Williams was notably active in coverage and part of the early pass rush pressure Steve Spagnuolo dialed up. The second-year cornerback has taken a significant step forward in his young career. Stock Up: Harrison Butker Butker made two field goals and all of his PATs in the victory, quieting the noise around his future as Kansas City's kicker. item.title: Leaked: 1st pictures of new Arsenal home kit for 2027/28
item.description: Leaked: 1st pictures of new Arsenal home kit for 2027/28 Arsenal’s home shirt for the 2027/28 season has leaked, with a few major changes compared to this year’s home kit. Photo via FootyHeadlines.com Footy Headlines have leaked the design of Arsenal’s home shirt for the 2027/28 season, revealing some changes from recent seasons. The main one is the use of a tonal vertical striped pattern. Arsenal have generally only used a very subtle pattern (if any) on the front of the home shirt for the last few campaigns, but this one is much more pronounced. Then there’s the change to the Emirates sponsor logo, which just reads “Emirates”, rather than including “Fly Better”. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images The shirt has also gone back to using the cannon logo, rather than the white crest on the 2025/26 and 2026/27 shirts. It also uses a v-neck collar, and there is very minor navy detailing on the collar and sleeves. Footy Headlines have revealed that the shirt will be accompanied by white shorts with red and navy trim, and red side stripes. The kit will use white socks with a dark navy hope and red ‘AFC’ lettering, and they’ve included a computer-generated mock-up of the full kit: Photo via FootyHeadlines.com As usual, the expectation is that the new kit will be released at the end of the current campaign. Whether or not it is released during the current campaign seemingly depends on whether Arsenal still have trophies to play for, as the Gunners have tended to stick with the existing shirt until the final game if they can still win something in it. If not, they’ve tended to show off the new kit in the final home game of the season. Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images For Premier League

item.description: Real Madrid v RC Celta de Vigo - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Thibaut Courtois has admitted he is baffled by what a goalkeeper must achieve to win the Ballon d'Or after being overlooked for the top prize in recent years. The Real Madrid number one expressed his frustration while also confirming his ultimate ambition to hang up his gloves in the Spanish capital. Frustration over individual awards Courtois has spoken candidly about the difficulties goalkeepers face in winning the Ballon d'Or , a trophy that has only been awarded to a shot-stopper once in history. Reflecting on his own career and the lack of recognition for his position, the Belgian international expressed a sense of resignation regarding the voting process. He pointed to 2022 as a year where he felt he deserved a higher ranking, noting that while Karim Benzema was a worthy winner, keepers are often relegated to the Yashin Trophy rather than the main prize. "I think I expected to be higher in 2022. Karim deserved it, but I think I should have been higher. We can perform brilliantly, but in the final minute [Kylian] Mbappe might score and that is what people will remember," explained Courtois, as quoted by AS . The veteran keeper, who recently extended his contract with the Merengues, highlighted that even standout seasons often fall short of the top individual honours. "It is difficult, I understand that, but I do not know what kind of season a goalkeeper has to have to win a Ballon d'Or. Some goalkeepers deserve to finish higher in the Ballon d'Or standings," he added. Commitment to Real Madrid Beyond his individual frustrations, Courtois made his long-term intentions clear by stating his desire to end his career at the Santiago Bernabeu. Having signed a contract extension, he emphasised that his primary goal is to remain healthy and continue winning trophies with the Spanish giants. "I'm very happy and proud to have signed for another year. My goal is to finish my career here; I need to stay healthy. I'm grateful for the club's confidence. The Champions League is tough, and with this format, everything is more open. I've won two, and I hope to win more," he confirmed. item.title: Mike Breen is still chasing a better call
item.description: Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Please don’t call Mike Breen the dean of NBA broadcasters. “This title of voice of the NBA that usually goes with whoever’s the NBA Finals announcer, I’ve never been comfortable with that,” he says. “Because I’m not the voice. There are so many voices.” Plus, there’s room for improvement. All the broadcasters in Breen’s circle want to get better. Yes, even the guy who has called the Finals since the second George W. Bush administration. “Every year I feel like I can get better at something, whether it’s having a more concise call, a better way to put into perspective what it means, the big picture stuff,” Breen says. This is not debatable. An NBA game feels important when Breen calls it. He’s at the point in his career – he’s called the Finals on TV since 2006; he’s been the voice of the Knicks (on radio, then TV) since 1991 – where he’s at the top of his profession. And that’s right: The Knicks, his boyhood team, are defending world champs after 53 years , thanks to a title run down a volcano, through a black hole, and over a rainbow. It’s all happening! item.title: New Zealand Rugby gives strong backing to Dave Rennie after record All Blacks defeat to England
item.description: New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has given its unequivocal backing to All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie through to the World Cup after back-to-back defeats to Wales and England. The tourists were stunned in Cardiff as Wales beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years, before suffering a record loss to England at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium on Saturday. Rennie was only appointed as Scott Robertson’s successor in March and took charge ahead of the Nations Championship in July, but has now suffered five defeats this year – including three to South Africa during the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour. NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster is clear, though, that the head coach retains their strong backing as the All Blacks prepare to meet England again this weekend. “We have complete confidence in Rens,” Lancaster said. “His position is not in question. He will take the team to the World Cup. That is not going to change. “He is a world-class coach. We went through the most rigorous appointment process that I have been involved in, which included spending time observing him coaching in Japan with his team and in his environment. “He is a very strong head coach. He provides absolute clarity to his team about how they want to play and absolute accountability about what is expected, what is measured. There are no gaps in information or understanding about the environment. The team love him. They are all behind him. They are all happy in the environment. The All Blacks suffered a record defeat to England (Getty) “Rens has incredible attention to detail. If you talk to Rens about the game he wants to play, he backs it all up by facts, evidence and data. Nothing is left to chance. Nothing is done on gut feel or assumption. He is in our mind the right man to take this team to the World Cup.” Rennie made a strong start to his tenure, beating France, Italy and Ireland in July before conquering the Springboks at Ellis Park in the first of a four-Test series. Two thrashings of Australia retained the Bledisloe Cup in October and Scotland were beaten in their November opener, but the head coach admitted his side “let the country down” after the Wales defeat. The squad have had to deal with the sudden passing of security chief Logan Cadwallader in Edinburgh, which is understood to have hit them hard, while the demands of a gruelling year of international action have also perhaps been felt. item.title: Saints vs. Bears: The good, the bad, and the ugly from Week 11
item.description: The Good: Defense All things considered the Saints defense played pretty well on Sunday. They held one of the better offenses in the NFL in the Bears to just 19 points and held Caleb Williams to 181 yards. The Saints defense also sacked Williams twice, and got four tackles for loss. They also got two takeaways, both through the efforts of Carl Granderson who tipped a pass that was intercepted by Danny Stutsman and forced a fumble that was recovered by Julian Blackmon. The Bad: Pass protection Tyler Shough was under duress all day as the Saints allowed 6 sacks. Shough had a hand in some of these as he left the pocket too early and scrambled into the defenders arms, but the Saints allowed Jeffrey Simmons to live in the backfield almost the whole game and allowed a total of 10 tackles for loss. item.description: Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers had a difficult afternoon as the Pittsburgh Steelers fell to a frustrating 19-16 defeat against the Philadelphia Eagles. item.title: The secret injury clause that has Bayern Munich freaking out over Jamal Musiala
item.description: (Photo by S. Mellar/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Talk about a masterclass in negotiation. When Bayern Munich signed Jamal Musiala onto a bumper contract in 2025, there was speculation surrounding the details. Most drew attention to his salary increase, but a certain secret clause inserted by the player’s camp now has FC Bayern in a bind. According to a report by Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ), Jamal Musiala has a special guarantee in his contract that allows him to earn his full salary for six months in the event of an injury. With the emerging revelations about Musiala’s neurological issues, this clause has become a major sticking point for FC Bayern. Why does this matter? Most people don’t know this, but when a player gets injured playing in the Bundesliga, the club only has to pay six weeks of guaranteed salary before insurance takes over. So, if Musiala were to miss more than six weeks, Bayern Munich would have been off the hook. If it was a regular contract. Instead, with this clause, Musiala is guaranteed to be paid his substantial wages for up to half a year in the event of illness or injury. This means that, if Musiala experiences another episode and misses several months of football, he would still cost the club millions of euros despite not being able to contribute on the pitch. This is not the first time a clause like this has been granted by FC Bayern. Manuel Neuer also had something similar in his previous contracts, and Alphonso Davies is rumored to have one as well (though for a shorter duration of 3-4 months). For Musiala, the clause is doing what it’s supposed to. It is giving the player a semblance of security during this uncertain period in his life. For Bayern, however, it is turning into a massive liability. This may go some ways to explain the strange behavior by the executive team in recent days, though it is unlikely to win them any sympathy. With so many millions of euros on the line, and Musiala’s contract running to 2030, Bayern Munich are in desperate need of a solution to a problem they agreed to have. Join the conversation! item.title: Syracuse football: Orange lose more than bowl opportunity in Boston
item.description: CHESTNUT HILL, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 21: Justus Ross-Simmons #86 of the Syracuse Orange makes a catch against the Boston College Eagles during the first half at Alumni Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images) | Getty Images If we’re being honest, there isn’t a ton of difference between 6-6 and 5-7….except where there is. After starting 2-4 and dealing with injuries to three quarterbacks, the Syracuse Orange had battled back and put themselves in position to end 2026 with a bowl bid. 6-6 would have shown fans that the team hadn’t quit and that maybe Fran Brown had earned some trust heading into 2027. Instead, Syracuse went to Boston College and watched as the familiar themes of this season: costly penalties, red-zone inefficiency and the nation’s worst kicking game resulted in a loss in a game the Orange had to have. Now it will take a Miracle on Irving Ave to get to 6-6 with a Notre Dame team that needs to make their final CFP case. 5-7 will be a point for those who want a new head coach. They will point to the California, Clemson and BC losses and say this team could have been 8-4….they will have a point there. The Orange gave away those three games and with them they would have had a solid bowl invitation. We can’t blame injuries for these games but Saturday’s game showed that Syracuse football needs to find ways to build depth. It also needs to stop giving away points with poor game management. At the end of the first half, simply running out a defensive sub when BC went into their fire-drill field goal scramble would have run out the half and saved three points. If you’re not down two scores, you take a short field goal (yes can’t assume it’ s a make) and maybe you get ahead of BC in the fourth instead of letting them continue to lead. If you’re worried about offensive plays in the red zone without your dynamic receiver duo of Hatcher and Russell, then call time out and tell the offensive coordinator to run something with them. If you notice your fifth-string running breathing heavy after a 29-yard run, get a substitute in and then run something different. Fans hate early timeouts but in games of this magnitude saving them for the final two minutes might not matter. (As an aside, there’s been this weird online conspiracy that Josh Gattis is calling the plays, but the funny part is all the people pushing this narrative weirdly still blame Jeff Nixon for red-zone play calling. Make that make sense) The next few weeks will be pivotal for Fran Brown. He’s got plenty of young players with game experience to build around, but he’s got to keep them, make the right call at quarterback, bolster the offensive line and figure out what he’s going to do with his coaching staff. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
